policy_note: Per AGENTS.md, macro views must not directly change any company's 100-point score. This overlay may change portfolio risk budget, scenario severity, valuation scrutiny, and evidence priority only.

regime.label: MODERATE_TO_STRONG_GROWTH_STICKY_INFLATION_HIGHER_FOR_LONGER_HIGH_GEOPOLITICAL_VOLATILITY
regime.summary: AI and infrastructure capex are supporting global growth, while energy/geopolitical shocks, fiscal pressure and still-elevated PCE inflation keep the policy and long-end-rate regime restrictive.

core_inferences.statement: The near-term U.S. base case is continued expansion rather than recession, although the 4.7% GDPNow reading should not be extrapolated as a sustainable trend rate.
Inflation is sufficiently above central-bank targets to constrain rapid easing, particularly while energy prices remain elevated.

Long-duration assets face a structural valuation headwind because U.S. long-term yields can remain elevated even without a large additional Fed hiking cycle, given strong nominal growth, fiscal deficits and high real yields.
evidence: debt held by public 101% of GDP

core_inferences.statement: AI and data-center capex remain a major global growth support, especially for the U.S., Korea, China high-tech exports and power infrastructure supply chains.
evidence: Korea August exports +68.7% with semiconductor exports +209%
Bank of Korea cites robust AI investment and semiconductor boom

core_inferences.statement: The largest six-month nonlinear macro risk is a sustained Middle-East energy shock that lifts inflation while reducing real household purchasing power.
evidence: shipping disruption and regional conflict risk

six_month_scenarios.name: BASE_STICKY_INFLATION_EXPANSION
six_month_scenarios.description: Growth remains positive, inflation declines only slowly, central banks remain restrictive and the Fed delivers limited additional tightening or prolonged holding rather than an easing cycle.
six_month_scenarios.market_implication: Earnings can grow, but equity multiple expansion is capped; quality and cash-return discipline matter more than duration.

six_month_scenarios.name: INFLATION_ENERGY_SHOCK
six_month_scenarios.description: Brent remains above roughly $105-$110 for a sustained period, second-round inflation rises and central banks tighten more than currently expected.
six_month_scenarios.market_implication: Long yields rise, long-duration growth assets and leveraged balance sheets de-rate, while pricing power and energy resilience gain value.

six_month_scenarios.name: DISINFLATIONARY_SOFT_LANDING
six_month_scenarios.description: Middle-East risk eases, energy falls, core inflation decelerates and policy expectations shift back toward eventual easing without a recession.
six_month_scenarios.market_implication: Duration and high-quality growth benefit; long bonds rally.

six_month_scenarios.name: GROWTH_OR_CREDIT_SHOCK
six_month_scenarios.description: AI capex slows sharply, trade/geopolitical stress or a credit event causes rapid risk-off and weaker growth.
six_month_scenarios.market_implication: Initial broad risk-off followed by falling policy/long rates; balance-sheet strength becomes dominant.

do: Prefer companies with high incremental ROIC, strong free-cash-flow conversion and low refinancing dependence.
Apply stricter reverse-DCF and hurdle-rate discipline to long-duration growth and acquisition-heavy companies.
Stress test energy, wage, materials and interest-cost pass-through rather than assuming disinflation.
Treat AI/data-center/power infrastructure demand as a real tailwind but separate demand growth from incremental cash ROIC.
Maintain liquidity and avoid leverage because yen carry unwind, oil shocks and long-rate spikes can create abrupt drawdowns.
do_not: Do not add or subtract points from company quality scores solely because the macro regime changes.
Do not infer a buy signal from sector tailwinds without valuation and company-specific cash-return evidence.
Do not assume Fed easing automatically implies a major decline in long-term yields.

regional_view.united_states: Expansion with inflation and long-rate pressure; AI capex offsets tighter financial conditions.
regional_view.euro_area: Growth has improved, but energy sensitivity keeps inflation and policy risk asymmetric to the upside.
regional_view.japan: BOJ normalization and yen strength raise global carry-unwind risk.
regional_view.south_korea: Semiconductor/AI export boom is a major cyclical tailwind; higher rates and imported-energy exposure are offsets.
regional_view.china: External/high-tech trade is strong while domestic demand and property remain weaker; trade-friction risk rises with surpluses.

watchlist.why_it_matters: Tests whether the energy shock is translating into another hiking phase.
First major test of whether energy pressure is passing through to broader inflation.
Determines whether the Fed converts July's internal hike pressure into actual tightening.
A hike could accelerate yen carry unwind and global risk-asset volatility.
Could materially revise recent U.S. growth and PCE history.

reassessment_triggers: Brent sustains above $110 or falls below $80
U.S. core PCE moves decisively below 2.8% or above 3.6% YoY
U.S. unemployment rises above 4.7% with negative payroll trend
U.S. 10-year Treasury sustains above 5.25% or falls below 4.25%
Fed begins a clear easing cycle or delivers more than 50bp additional tightening
AI/data-center capex guidance weakens materially across hyperscalers
China-U.S. trade truce materially breaks down
Korean semiconductor exports or order indicators reverse sharply
limitations: Scenario probabilities are analyst judgments, not observable facts.
Point-in-time oil, yield and market-implied policy probabilities can change intraday.
GDPNow is a model nowcast, not an official GDP forecast or realized result.
CBO fiscal figures are February 2026 baseline projections and may not incorporate later legislation.
Macro views affect portfolio risk budgeting and scenario assumptions, not company-quality scoring.
